headline: This $20,250 roof quote is about 35% higher than usual.
summary: Premier Valley Roofing wants $20,250 to replace a roof of about 1,800 sq ft. A typical price in the LA area is about $12,500 to $17,500. The quote has no California contractor license number and asks for a $8,100 deposit up front, which is much more than the law allows. Don't sign today.
if_ignored: Nothing bad happens if you don't sign. The "today only" price is a pressure tactic. Take your time and get 2 or 3 other quotes.

action_steps.title: Don't sign or pay today
action_steps.detail: A "price good today only" offer is a common pressure tactic. A fair contractor will give you time to decide.

action_steps.title: Ask for their license number and check it
action_steps.detail: Roof work this big needs a California contractor license. Ask for the number, then look it up for free on the CSLB website.

action_steps.title: Get 2–3 more quotes
action_steps.detail: Ask other licensed roofers to quote the same job: tear-off, 18 squares of architectural shingles, underlayment and flashing. Compare line by line.

action_steps.title: Never pay a big deposit
action_steps.detail: In California, the deposit for home improvement work can't be more than 10% of the price or $1,000, whichever is less. For this job, that's $1,000 at most, not $8,100.

red_flags.text: No California contractor license number on the quote. Work over $500 needs a CSLB license.
They want a 40% deposit ($8,100). The legal limit is $1,000 for this job.
"Misc materials" for $2,400 is vague. Ask exactly what it covers.
"Special price good today only" is pressure to sign fast.
A discount for cash can mean no paper trail. Pay by check or card so you have proof.
No start date, finish date or written warranty.

line_items.item: Flashing, drip edge, pipe boots & ridge vents

questions_to_ask: What is your California contractor license number?
What exactly is in the $2,400 "misc materials"? Can you list it?
Shingle installation already includes labor. What is the extra $1,750 labor for?
Can we do a $1,000 deposit, with the rest paid as the work is finished, and a written warranty?
